references.text: Earlier in the same chapter, the command is given to give the Levites cities to live in with surrounding pasturelands.
The next verse further clarifies the measurements for the pastureland, specifying two thousand cubits on each side from the outer edge of the city.
The laws concerning the Levitical cities and their pasturelands, which establish that the Levites always have the right of redemption and that the pasturelands cannot be sold.
The fulfillment of the command regarding the Levitical cities, where the Levites come to Joshua and ask for cities with pasturelands as the Lord had commanded through Moses.
A summary of the Levitical cities, stating that each city had pasturelands around it, in accordance with the command in Numbers.
The parallel account in Chronicles regarding the Levitical cities with their associated pasturelands given to the descendants of Aaron.
Ezekiel's vision of the future temple area includes an open space of fifty cubits around the sanctuary, reflecting the principle of pastureland surrounding holy areas.
In Ezekiel's vision concerning the division of the land, the Levites receive an area that is not to be sold or exchanged, corresponding to the principle of the Levites' inalienable pasturelands.
